levels.title_en: Two forms that collide with something else

items.pronunciation_notes: Identical in sound to the continuous marker, and only position tells them apart: ra-haa.
items.gloss_en: रहना's perfective, which looks like the continuous marker

learn.explanation_en: रहना is regular, so its perfective is रहा — which is spelled and pronounced exactly like the continuous marker you have been using since level eight. वह यहाँ रहा means he stayed here, and there is no continuous anywhere in it. The way to keep them apart is position: the marker always sits between a bare stem and an auxiliary, as in वह रह रहा था, while the participle stands where a verb stands. If रहा has a stem in front of it, it is the marker. If it does not, it is the verb.

examples.note: The perfective participle of रहना, standing alone as the verb.
Two रह sounds — the first is the stem, the second is the marker.
The participle agrees like any other, and so does the marker.

common_error.why_en: The bare stem comes first and the marker second. Reversing them separates the verb from its own ending.

practice.prompt_en: Conjugate the verb for this subject.
practice.question: रहना · वह · masculine · simple past
practice.explanation_en: The bare perfective of रहना is रहा, with no stem in front of it.

game.question_en: Which form belongs in the continuous past cell?
game.explanation_en: वह यहाँ रह रहा था — stem, marker, auxiliary, in that order.

items.pronunciation_notes: Two short vowels with nothing between them: ki-e.
items.gloss_en: the irregular participles take ordinary agreement

learn.explanation_en: The four transitive irregulars are odd only in their stems. Their endings are the same four you have used all module: किया, की, किए, कीं. Same for लिया, ली, लिए, लीं and दिया, दी, दिए, दीं. So there is nothing new to learn about the agreement — but there is something to know about what it agrees with. In Module 9 these participles will agree with the object of the sentence rather than the subject, which is the opposite of everything this module has taught. That is why they are recognition only for now: you can read them, and the rule for choosing between them changes before you can write them.

examples.note: Masculine plural, built exactly like गए and आए.
The same ending on another of the four.

common_error.why_en: A transitive perfective needs ने on the subject, and the participle then agrees with the object rather than with वह. Both halves of that arrive in Module 9.

practice.question: करना · masculine plural · perfective
practice.explanation_en: The stem is irregular but the plural ending is the ordinary -ए.

game.question_en: Which form belongs in the habitual present cell?
game.explanation_en: वह करता है. The participle किए cannot yet stand in a sentence of its own.

items.pronunciation_notes: One long syllable, identical in sound to the possessive marker: kii.
items.gloss_en: the participle that is spelled like a postposition

learn.title_en: की is a verb and also a postposition
learn.explanation_en: The feminine perfective of करना is की, spelled exactly like the possessive marker from Module 6. Two completely unrelated words, one spelling. In practice they are easy to separate, because the possessive sits between two nouns — राम की किताब — while the participle stands where a verb stands, at the end of a clause. Worth knowing now rather than being surprised by it in reading, since करना is the most common verb in the language and its feminine perfective turns up constantly.

examples.note: The feminine perfective participle of करना, in citation.
The possessive from Module 6, between two nouns.
The possessive fused onto a pronoun, where no confusion can arise.

common_error.why_en: The possessive needs the thing possessed behind it. Standing alone at the end of a phrase, की would be read as the verb instead.

practice.question: करना · feminine singular · perfective
practice.explanation_en: की, with the same irregular stem as किया and the ordinary feminine ending.

game.question_en: Which form belongs in the continuous present cell?
game.explanation_en: वह कर रही है — she is doing it right now.

summary.recap_en: रहा is both the perfective of रहना and the continuous marker, told apart by whether a bare stem stands in front of it. की is both the feminine perfective of करना and the possessive from Module 6, told apart by whether a noun follows it. The irregular participles are odd only in their stems — the endings are the ones you already know.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the last level, where the grid is pulled back together and the only remaining question is which cell you want.

items.pronunciation_notes: रोज़ has a dotted ज़ pronounced as a z, and a long open o: roz.

learn.title_en: रोज़ can only take the habitual
learn.explanation_en: Thirty-one levels of forms are worth very little if you cannot pick the right one under pressure, so this last level is about choosing rather than building. The most reliable guide is the adverb. रोज़, हमेशा, कभी — anything meaning repeatedly — can only sit with the habitual, because a repeated action is precisely what that aspect describes. वह रोज़ जाता है is correct and वह रोज़ जा रहा है is not, however natural the continuous may feel. When you are unsure which cell you want, look at the time word first and let it decide.

examples.note: रोज़ forces the habitual and rules out everything else.

examples.english: he used to go every day
examples.note: The same aspect, moved one column into the past.
And the third column — a guess about the same habit.

common_error.why_en: The continuous describes one stretch of time in progress, which cannot be something that happens every day.

practice.prompt_en: Choose the form that fits the sentence.
practice.question: वह रोज़ ___
practice.explanation_en: रोज़ describes a repeated action, so only the habitual can follow it.

game.question_en: Which form belongs in the habitual presumptive cell?
game.explanation_en: वह रोज़ जाता होगा — a habit offered as a guess.

items.pronunciation_notes: अभी has a breathy bh and a long ii at the end: a-bhii.
items.gloss_en: a word meaning now forces the continuous

learn.title_en: अभी can only take the continuous
learn.explanation_en: The test works in the other direction too. अभी means right now, and it can only sit with an action in progress, so वह अभी जा रहा है is the only possibility. This is the pair that has been running through the whole module — habitual against continuous, वह जाता है against वह जा रहा है — and it is the distinction English speakers get wrong most often, because English lets goes and is going blur into each other in a way Hindi does not. Two adverbs, two cells, and between them they resolve most of the uncertainty you will meet.

examples.note: अभी pins the sentence to this moment.
The same aspect one column back — a moment in the past.
Another verb, and the adverb still decides the aspect.

common_error.why_en: The habitual is a fact about his routine and says nothing about this moment, which is exactly what अभी is asking about.

practice.prompt_en: Choose the form that fits the sentence.
practice.question: वह अभी ___
practice.explanation_en: अभी means at this moment, and only the continuous describes something in progress.

game.question_en: Which form belongs in the continuous past cell?
game.explanation_en: वह अभी जा रहा था — he was going a moment ago.

items.pronunciation_notes: कल is one short flat syllable and carries no stress: kal.
items.gloss_en: a named past time forces the bare perfective

learn.title_en: कल takes the bare perfective, and the module is done
learn.explanation_en: Name a past time and the bare perfective is what follows: वह कल गया. Not गया है, which would tie the result to now and clash with कल, and not गया था, which would need a later past moment to measure against. This is the third adverb test and it completes a small toolkit — रोज़ for the habitual, अभी for the continuous, कल for the bare perfective. That covers most ordinary sentences. What the module leaves you with is smaller than it looks: two participles, one marker, three sets of auxiliaries, one set of future endings, and three imperatives. Everything else was agreement you already knew from Module 6.

examples.note: A named past time, so the bare form with no auxiliary.
कल means both yesterday and tomorrow — the verb is what tells you which.
The same shape with feminine agreement.

common_error.why_en: है ties the result to the present moment, which contradicts कल pointing back at yesterday.

practice.prompt_en: Choose the form that fits the sentence.
practice.question: वह कल ___ (यह बीत चुका है)
practice.explanation_en: A named past time takes the bare perfective, with no auxiliary behind it.

game.question_en: Which form belongs in the perfective past cell?
game.explanation_en: वह कल गया था — he had gone, measured back from some later past moment.

summary.recap_en: Three adverbs settle most of the choosing: रोज़ takes the habitual, अभी takes the continuous, and a named past time like कल takes the bare perfective. The module itself reduces to two participles, one continuous marker, three sets of auxiliaries, one set of future endings and three imperatives — everything else was agreement carried over from Module 6.
summary.next_up_en: Module 7 is complete, and with it Phase 3. Every tense in the language is now available to you with one exception: transitive verbs in the perfective, which need ने. That is Module 9, and it is the single highest-value thing left to learn.
